questions.q: What problem does delegated administration solve?
options: It eliminates the need for any administrative roles at all
It avoids the choice between refusing routine admin requests and over-granting full admin for narrow tasks
It replaces the sys_user_has_role table with a new mechanism
It only applies to Service Catalog configuration
questions.explain: Without scoped roles, every administrative request forces a bad tradeoff: become a bottleneck, or hand out more power than the task needs.

questions.q: Which scoped role is designed for managing user records and group membership without full admin access?
options: report_admin
catalog_admin
user_admin
itil_admin
questions.explain: user_admin covers creating and editing user records and managing group membership — the common need of an HR-adjacent manager or helpdesk lead.

questions.q: A catalog owner needs to build and maintain Service Catalog items and variable sets. Which role fits best, per least privilege?
options: admin
catalog_admin
report_admin
user_admin
questions.explain: catalog_admin grants exactly the Service Catalog management power needed, without reaching into user administration or reporting.

questions.q: Why should you still check a scoped role's Contains Roles list before assigning it, even though it sounds narrow?
options: You never need to check this for scoped roles, only for admin
Scoped roles can never be customized, so this step is pointless
In a heavily customized instance, a scoped role could have been configured to contain more than its name implies
Contains Roles only applies to the itil role
questions.explain: The containment-checking habit from Lesson 3 doesn't stop applying just because a role name sounds narrower.

questions.q: Per this lesson, when is granting full admin actually the right call?
options: Whenever any administrative request comes in, since it's the simplest option
Never, under any circumstances
Only when a request genuinely spans multiple administrative domains at once, or no scoped role exists and building one isn't practical
Only for users who already hold the itil role
questions.explain: Defaulting to admin because it's familiar is actually the riskier choice — it should be reserved for genuinely cross-domain platform-owner needs.
